safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الملأ): its i'rab has already been given [Note: in āya (29) of this sūra.]; the nūn in (أفتوني) is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya); (في أمري) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أفتوني); (أمرا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle قاطعة [Note: or accusative by removal of the preposition, the original being قاطعة في أمر, i.e. "deciding upon it".]; (حتّى) is a particle of limit and a preposition; (تشهدون) is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتّى, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the (nūn) is for protection before the first-person yāʾ, which is dropped for the sake of the verse-ending (fāṣila).
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The vocative clause and its answer ... are in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «أفتوني ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «ما كنت قاطعة ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or causal (taʿlīliyya) —; the clause «تشهدون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن), and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تشهدوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by (حتّى), attached to the active participle قاطعة.

* Morphology:
(قاطعة): feminine of قاطع, the active participle of the triliteral قطع; its pattern is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:33-33.t:
* I'rab:
(أولو): a nominative khabar (predicate), the sign of the nominative being the wāw, since it is attached (mulḥaq) to the sound masculine plural; the second (أولو) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first; (إليك) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) الأمر; (الفاء) links to the apodosis of an implied condition; (ماذا تأمرين) is like ماذا يرجعون [Note: in āya (28) of this sūra.].
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «نحن أولو ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «الأمر إليك ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «انظري ...» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you resolve upon a matter, then consider".
The clause «تأمرين ...» is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of considering, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative; the verb has the sense of reflecting.

* Rhetoric:
Concision (al-ījāz): in the words of Allah the Exalted قالُوا نَحْنُ أُولُوا قُوَّةٍ وَأُولُوا بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ وَالْأَمْرُ إِلَيْكِ فَانْظُرِي ماذا تَأْمُرِينَ there is a wondrous concision: first, it indicates the high regard for consultation and Bilqīs's high regard for the counsellor; second, it indicates their high regard for her command and their obedience to her. In their saying «وَالْأَمْرُ إِلَيْكِ» and their saying «فَانْظُرِي ماذا تَأْمُرِينَ» there is a concision that intoxicates the minds. Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn al-Ṭayyib al-Bāqillānī said in his book Iʿjāz al-Qurʾān: "Speech may be spoiled and obscured by lightening and condensing it, but this is something that brevity only makes more expansive, because it is firmly placed and falls in its proper place; and its concision contains a versatility that goes beyond its place and position." Until he says: "You will find in all that we have recited to you nothing but what, when expanded, is informative; when abridged, is complete and excellent in its kind; and when the sage sends the glance of his mind across its sides, and the learned man dispatches the eyes of his inquiries into its corners, he lights only upon beauties following one another and marvels in succession."

* Benefits:
1- أولو ...
It is a plural meaning «ذوو», i.e. "possessors of", with no singular of its own. It has also been said to be a collective noun (ism jamʿ) whose singular is «ذو» meaning "possessor"; in that it is declined by letters, it is attached (mulḥaq) to the sound masculine plural.
Its feminine is «أولات» and its singular «ذات». The words attached to this plural have already been discussed, so return to that in its place in this book.
2- ماذا ...
«ماذا» has been discussed in more than one place; we return to summarise for you what Ibn Hishām says on the matter, because of its usefulness:
Ibn Hishām holds that «ماذا» has four aspects:
The first: that «ما» be interrogative and «ذا» a demonstrative, as in «ماذا الوقوف؟» ("what is this standing?").
The second: that «ما» be interrogative and «ذا» a relative noun, as in the verse of Labīd:
ألا تسألان المرء ماذا يحاول ... أنحبّ فيقضي أم ضلال وباطل
(Will you two not ask a man what it is he strives for — a vow he fulfils, or error and falsehood?)
As in your saying: لماذا جئت؟ ("why did you come?")
[Translator's note: the text passes from the second aspect directly to the fourth; the third aspect is missing in the source, and the example «لماذا جئت؟» appears to belong to it.]
The fourth: that «ماذا» as a whole be a generic noun meaning "something", or a relative noun meaning "that which". There is disagreement over the poet's words:
دعي ماذا علمت سأتقيه ... ولكن بالمغيّب نبيئني
(Leave what you know — I will guard against it; but tell me of what is hidden.)

safi-cedvel:34-35.t:
* I'rab:
(أذلّة): the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), its governor being جعلوا; (الواو) is a conjunction — or resumptive —; (كذلك) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is يفعلون [Note: it may also be attached to the verb يفعلون if the pronoun refers to the kings, the speech then being a resumption from Allah the Exalted]; the wāw in (يفعلون) refers to the senders of the letter.
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الملوك ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The conditional clause and its apodosis are in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «دخلوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أفسدوها ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «جعلوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «يفعلون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هؤلاء" [Note: the clause may be resumptive if it is the word of Allah the Exalted rather than part of her speech.], and the nominal clause هؤلاء يفعلون is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
a conjunction; (ناظرة) is conjoined to مرسلة, nominative; (بم) is attached to (يرجع), and ما is an interrogative noun whose alif has been dropped because the preposition entered upon it.
[Translator's note: the beginning of the i'rab of āya 35 has been displaced in the source into the Morphology section below (the line beginning «(35)»); the fragment "a conjunction" here continues from it, i.e. (الفاء) is a conjunction.]
The clause «إنّي مرسلة ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «يرجع المرسلون» is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of the active participle ناظرة, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative [Note: i.e. awaiting the return of the envoys and with what reply they will come back.].

* Morphology:
(أعزّة): plural of عزيز, a ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle) from the triliteral verb عزّ, of the ضرب class; its pattern is فعيل and the plural أفعلة; there are other plurals: عزاز with kasra on the ʿayn, and أعزّاء on the pattern أفعلاء — with a doubled zāy —.
(35) (الواو) is a conjunction; (إليهم) is attached to مرسلة; (بهديّة) is attached to مرسلة; (الفاء) (مرسلة): feminine of مرسل, the active participle of the quadriliteral (أرسل); its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(ناظرة): feminine of ناظر, the active participle of the triliteral (نظر); its pattern is فاعل.
(هديّة): feminine of هديّ, a noun for what is given out of generosity and the like; its plurals are هدايا and هداوى.

safi-cedvel:38-38.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أيّها الملأ): its i'rab has already been given [Note: in āya (29) of this sūra.]; (أيكم) is an interrogative noun, a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject); (بعرشها) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأتيني); (قبل) is an accusative adverb, attached to (يأتيني); (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; the nūn in (يأتوني) is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya); (مسلمين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يأتوني ...) is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The vocative clause and its answer ... are in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «أيّكم يأتيني ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «يأتيني ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (أيّكم).
The clause «يأتوني ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(من الجن) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of عفريت; (آتيك) is a nominative imperfect verb, the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma ... and (الكاف) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: it may be an active participle, a nominative khabar (predicate) ... with the kāf as muḍāf ilayhi.]; (به) is attached to (آتيك); (قبل) is an accusative adverb attached to (آتيك); (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (من مقامك) is attached to (تقوم).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تقوم ...) is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
(الواو) is the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (عليه) is attached to قويّ, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "for carrying it"; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (أمين) is a second khabar.
The clause «قال عفريت ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أنا آتيك ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «آتيك به» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (أنا).
The clause «تقوم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «إنّي عليه لقوي ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl [Note: or in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.].

* Morphology:
(عفريت): a noun for one of the jinn, or an adjective describing one; its pattern is فعليل, with kasra then sukūn, and it is derived from the verb تعفرت.

safi-cedvel:36-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (لمّا) is an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of a condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis قال; the fāʿil (agent) of (جاء) is a pronoun referring to the queen's envoy; (سليمان) is an accusative mafʿūl bihi (direct object), barred from nunation because it is a proper name with an added alif and nūn; (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke; the second nūn in (تمدّونن) is for protection (wiqāya) before the first-person yāʾ, which is dropped for lightness; (بمال) is attached to the verb تمدّونن; (الفاء) is causal (taʿlīliyya); (ما) is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject) in the position of the nominative, its khabar (predicate) being (خير); (ممّا) is attached to خير; (بل) is for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (بهديّتكم) is attached to (تفرحون).
The clause «جاء ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تمدّونن ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «ما آتاني الله ...» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «آتاني الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (ما).
The clause «آتاكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «أنتم ... تفرحون» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «تفرحون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).
(37) (إليهم) is attached to (ارجع); (الفاء) links to the apodosis of an implied condition; (اللام) is the lām of the oath for an implied oath; (نأتينّهم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative ... (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and (هم) is a pronoun, the mafʿūl bihi; (بجنود) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of نأتينّ; (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (قبل) is the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of the accusative; (لهم) is attached to the khabar of lā, and likewise (بها); (الواو) is a conjunction; (لنخرجنّهم) is like لنأتينّهم; (منها) is attached to (نخرجنّهم); (أذلّة) is an accusative ḥāl; (الواو) is the wāw of the ḥāl ...
The clause «ارجع ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The implied oath clause ... is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if they do not come to me in submission, then by Allah we shall surely come to them ...".
The clause «نأتينّهم ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath.
The clause «لا قبل لهم ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of جنود.
The clause «نخرجنّهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نأتينّهم.
The clause «هم صاغرون» is in the position of the accusative as an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida).

* Benefits:
1- The two nūns of emphasis ...
a- They are the heavy nūn of emphasis and the light nūn of emphasis. Both occur together in the words of Allah the Exalted: لَيُسْجَنَنَّ وَلَيَكُوناً.
b- Which verbs are emphasised and which are not:
1- The imperative is emphasised with them without restriction, e.g. أكرمنّ جارك ("be sure to honour your neighbour"), and likewise the supplication, as in his words «فأنزلن سكينة علينا» ("so send down tranquillity upon us").
2- The past tense is never emphasised with them.
3- The imperfect is emphasised with them, and has six cases with regard to such emphasis, for which we refer you to the longer works.
c- The ruling on the ending of the verb emphasised with them:
1- When we emphasise the verb with one of the two nūns of emphasis, and it is predicated of an overt noun or of the masculine singular pronoun, its ending takes fatḥa because the nūn directly adjoins it, and nothing is dropped from it, whether it is sound-final or weak-final, e.g. «وَلَيَنْصُرَنَّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ». However, the nūn of the nominative is dropped for the jussive-governing and accusative-governing particle in the five verbs (al-afʿāl al-khamsa).
2- When the emphasised verb is predicated of the feminine-plural nūn, an alif is added between the two nūns, the nūn of the women and the nūn of emphasis.
3- When the emphasised verb is predicated of the wāw of the group or the yāʾ of the addressed feminine: if it is sound, the nūn of the nominative is dropped for the accusative-governing or jussive-governing particle; if it is nominative, it is dropped because of the succession of identical letters; and the wāw of the group or the yāʾ of the addressee is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters — e.g. «لتنصرنّ يا قوم» ("you shall surely help, O people") and «لتجلسنّ يا هند» ("you shall surely sit, O Hind").
d- The light nūn differs from the heavy one in four rulings:
First — it does not occur after the alif that separates it from the feminine-plural nūn, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, so you do not say «اسعينان».
Second — it does not occur after the alif of the dual, for the reason of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
Third — it is dropped when followed by a quiescent letter, as in the words of al-Aḍbaṭ ibn Qurayʿ:
لا تهين الفقير علّك أن ... تركع يوما والدهر قد رفعه
(Do not despise the poor man; perhaps one day you will bow down while fate has raised him up.)
Fourth — in pause it is given the ruling of tanwīn, so when it comes after a fatḥa it is turned into an alif, e.g. «لنفسعا ولنكونا».
[Translator's note: «لنفسعا» is as printed in the source; the Quranic word (al-ʿAlaq 96:15) is لَنَسْفَعًا.]
We have alluded to some of the particulars of their rulings earlier in this book, and we also point out that there are detailed treatments of them in the longer works, so return to them and take patience as a shield, seeking benefit.

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(عنده) is an accusative adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) علم; (من الكتاب) is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of علم; (أنا آتيك ... يرتدّ): the i'rab of its counterpart has been given [Note: in the previous āya (39).]; (إليك) is attached to (يرتدّ).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يرتدّ ...) is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
(الفاء) is resumptive; (لمّا رآه ... قال) is like لمّا جاء ... قال [Note: in āya (36) of this sūra.]; (هذا) is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ; (من فضل) is a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar; (اللام) is for causation (taʿlīl); (يبلوني) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and the nūn is for protection (wiqāya).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبلوني) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to the maṣdar فضل or to an omitted verb, its implied form being "فضّل" ...
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative; (أم) is a conjunction correlated with the hamza; (الواو) is resumptive; (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّما) is the restrictive (kāffa) and restricted (makfūfa); (لنفسه) is attached to (يشكر); (الواو) is a conjunction; (من) is like the first; (الفاء) links to the apodosis; (كريم) is a nominative second khabar.
The clause «قال الذي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «عنده علم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «أنا آتيك ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «آتيك به ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنا).
The clause «يرتدّ إليك طرفك ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «رآه مستقرّا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «هذا من فضل ...» is in the position of the accusative as the second maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «يبلوني ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أشكر ...» is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of the yāʾ in (يبلوني).
The clause «أكفر ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause أشكر.
The clause «من شكر ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «شكر ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «إنّما يشكر ...» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «من كفر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause من شكر.
The clause «كفر ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «إنّ ربّي غنّي ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(مستقرّا): active participle of the six-letter (استقرّ); its pattern is مستفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (al-kināya): in the words of Allah the Exalted قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ.
It is a metonymy for speed. الطرف is the movement of your eyelids when you look; it was put in place of looking, and since the one looking is described as sending forth his glance, he is described as returning the glance, and the glance is described as returning. On this is the poet's saying:
وكنت إذا أرسلت طرفك رائدا ... لقلبك أتعبتك المناظر
(Whenever you sent your glance out as a scout for your heart, the sights wearied you.)

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(لها) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نكّروا); (ننظر) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the request, and the fāʿil (agent) is "نحن"; (الهمزة) is for the interrogative; (أم) is a conjunction correlated with the hamza; (من الذين) is attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of تكون; (لا) is negating.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نكّروا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «ننظر ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ, i.e. "if you disguise [it], we shall see ...".
The clause «تهتدي ...» is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of seeing, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «تكون ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause تهتدي.
The clause «لا يهتدون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).

safi-cedvel:42-42.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive; (لمّا جاءت قيل) is like لمّا رآه ... قال [Note: in āya (36) of this sūra.]; (الهمزة) is for the interrogative; (هكذا) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) عرشك; (هو) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as the khabar of كأنّ; (الواو) is a conjunction — or resumptive —, and (نا) is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: this pronoun may refer to Bilqīs, i.e. she went on to say: we were given knowledge of Sulaymān's prophethood before this miracle ... or it may refer to Sulaymān, the speech then being resumptive.]; (العلم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) — originally the second —; (من قبلها) is attached to the verb أوتينا; (الواو) is a conjunction ...
The clause «جاءت ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قيل ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «هكذا عرشك ...» is in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil [Note: it is originally the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech) clause.].
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «كأنّه هو ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «أوتينا ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause [Note: or it has no grammatical position, being resumptive; each of the two analyses depends on how the first-person pronoun in (أوتينا) is understood, as stated in footnote (2).].
The clause «كنّا مسلمين» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause أوتينا.

* Rhetoric:
The secret of the simile in the words of Allah the Exalted كَأَنَّهُ هُوَ:
A free simile (tashbīh mursal), to which she turned away from what the question required — which was that she say "it is it" — for a very subtle secret: «كأنه» expresses how close the resemblance was in her view, to the point that she made herself doubt whether the two things were different, so that she almost said "it is it"; and that was the state of Bilqīs. As for "هكذا هو" ("it is thus"), it is the expression of one who is certain that the two things are different and judges only that there is a resemblance between them. For this reason she turned to the expression mentioned in the recitation, because it matched her state.

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of صدّ; (من دون) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted resumptive pronoun; (من قوم) is attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of كانت; (كافرين) is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «صدها ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كانت تعبد ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «تعبد ...» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانت.
The clause «إنّها كانت ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «كانت من قوم ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:44-44.t:
* I'rab:
(لها) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قيل); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لجّة) is the accusative second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (عن ساقيها) is attached to (كشفت), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ since it is a dual; (ممرّد) is a nominative naʿt (adjective) of صرح; (من قوارير) is attached to a second naʿt of صرح; (ربّ) is the one addressed in the vocative, a muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ, which is dropped for lightness, and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi; (مع) is an accusative adverb attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of أسلمت; (لله) is attached to (أسلمت); (ربّ) is a genitive naʿt of the Name of Majesty.
The clause «قيل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ادخلي ...» is in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: because it is originally the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).].
The clause «رأته ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «حسبته ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «كشفت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause حسبته.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «إنّه صرح ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The vocative clause ... has no grammatical position: parenthetical, of supplication.
The clause «إنّي ظلمت ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «ظلمت نفسي ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «أسلمت ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause ظلمت.

* Morphology:
(الصرح): a non-derived (jāmid) noun for a palace or the courtyard of a house; its pattern is فعل.
(لجّة): a noun for water or for its waves; its pattern is فعلة with ḍamma then sukūn; its ʿayn and lām are the same letter.
(ساقيها): dual of ساق, a noun for the well-known limb; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas, and it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion: its origin is سوق with fatḥa on the sīn and the wāw; when the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa it was converted to an alif. Its plural is سوق, pattern فعل with ḍamma then sukūn, and سيقان and أسوق with fatḥa on the hamza and ḍamma on the wāw; ساق is usually feminine in form.
(ممرّد): passive participle of the quadriliteral (مرّد), i.e. "made smooth"; its pattern is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(قوارير): plural of قارورة, a noun for a glass vessel; its pattern is فاعولة, and the pattern of قوارير is فواعيل. They were so named because things settle (taqirru) inside them; in the āya its material, i.e. glass, is meant.

* Rhetoric:
Paronomasia (al-tajnīs): it is the agreement of two words in the arrangement of their letters, and here it is in the words of Allah the Exalted أَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمانَ

* Benefits:
1- It has been said that Sulaymān married Bilqīs, the queen of Yemen ...
He used to visit her once a month and stay with her for three days. She bore him children, and he confirmed her over her kingdom ... Other things have also been said: they claimed that Sulaymān married her to Dhū Tubbaʿ, one of the kings of Yemen, who are the Adhwāʾ ... !
2- الصرح ...
It is related in the books of tafsīr that Sulaymān ordered a palace to be built for Bilqīs on her route to him, and asked that this palace be of white glass, with water flowing beneath it, into which fish and other sea creatures were placed. Then Sulaymān's throne was placed at the head of the hall. When she saw the water as a deep pool she was afraid and thought that it was intended to drown her; she looked at Sulaymān's seat upon the water and was astonished; then she found herself compelled to cross the water, so she uncovered her shins. Through this it was intended to test her intelligence and to display the miracles to her — not, as some claim, that Sulaymān wished to verify whether there was hair on her shins, for that does not befit the station of prophethood and its elevation above base matters.

safi-cedvel:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (اللام) is the lām of the oath for an implied oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (إلى ثمود) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا); (صالحا) is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to (أخاهم); (أن) is an explicative particle [Note: or a maṣdar-forming particle ... and the interpreted maṣdar (أن اعبدوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted bāʾ, attached to (أرسلنا).], and it has been vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (إذا) is a particle of surprise (fujāʾa).
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «اعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position: explicative [Note: or it has no grammatical position as the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).].
The clause «هم فريقان ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer of the oath.
The clause «يختصمون» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of (فريقان).

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(قوم) is the one addressed in the vocative, a muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ, which is dropped for lightness, and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi; (لم) is a preposition and an interrogative noun whose alif is dropped, in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تستعجلون); (بالسيّئة) is attached to the verb تستعجلون, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "by seeking evil"; (قبل) is an adverb of time attached to (تستعجلون); (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); (لعلّكم) is a particle of hope that governs the accusative; the wāw in (ترحمون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «قال..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The vocative clause and its answer ... are in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «تستعجلون» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «تستغفرون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لعلّكم ترحمون» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «ترحمون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.

safi-cedvel:47-47.t:
* I'rab:
(بك) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اطّيّرنا), and likewise (بمن); (معك) is an accusative adverb attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من; (عند) is an accusative adverb attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (طائركم); (بل) is for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); the wāw in (تفتنون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اطّيّرنا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «طائركم عند الله ...» is in the position of the accusative as the second maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «أنتم قوم ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «تفتنون» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.

* Benefits:
- قالُوا اطَّيَّرْنا بِكَ وَبِمَنْ مَعَكَ ...
We have spoken about ṭiyara (taking evil omens) earlier in this book, and about the view of Islam on it, so there is no need to return to it and discuss it. Go back to it in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf in this book.

safi-cedvel:48-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (في المدينة) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of كان; (في الأرض) is attached to (يفسدون); (لا) is negating.
The clause «كان في المدينة تسعة ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يفسدون ...» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of (تسعة ...) [Note: or in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of رهط.].
The clause «لا يصلحون» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يفسدون.

* Rhetoric:
Completion (al-tamām or al-tatmīm): in the words of Allah the Exalted وَلا يُصْلِحُونَ. This device consists in placing in speech a word which, if removed from it, would diminish its meaning in itself or in its qualities, while the wording remains complete.
For His saying «وَكانَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍ يُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ»: their concern was pure corruption, and they were, as is related, brutal and coarse; it was they who advised the hamstringing of the she-camel, to spite Ṣāliḥ and provoke his anger; among them was Qudār ibn Sālif, famous for ill omen, who has been mentioned before. But His saying يفسدون في الأرض does not exclude that some rare good might come from them or from one of them, so He completed the speech with His saying «وَلا يُصْلِحُونَ», to rule out that such an excuse might occur, or that some minds might be stirred by doubt that it would occur. By this every hope of their affair being set right and their condition becoming good was cut off.

* Benefits:
- The tamyīz (specification) of numbers, and their masculine and feminine forms:
a- If the tamyīz of the number — between three and ten — is a generic noun (ism jins) or a collective noun (ism jamʿ) that has no singular from its own root, such as قوم and رهط, it is put in the genitive with «من», so we say: «عشرة من القوم لقيتهم» ("ten of the people I met"); and Allah the Exalted said: فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِنَ الطَّيْرِ. It may also be put in the genitive by annexing the number to it, as in: «وَكانَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍ».
b- If the tamyīz of the number «from three to ten and what is between them» is a plural, we annex the number to it, so it is genitive by annexation, e.g. ثلاثة رجال ("three men") and ثلاث نساء ("three women").
c- As for masculine and feminine, with collective and generic nouns this is judged according to their status, by considering whether the pronoun referring to them is masculine or feminine.
The number is given the opposite of what their pronoun requires in femininity and masculinity: if the pronoun is feminine, the number is masculine, and if it is masculine, the number is feminine; so we say: ثلاثة من الغنم عندي ("I have three sheep").
We made the number feminine because we make the pronoun of الغنم masculine, saying: غنم كثير. And we say: ثلاث من البط ("three ducks"), because we say بط كثيرة. But we say ثلاث or ثلاثة من البقر, because البقر and its pronoun may be either masculine or feminine. d- The collective noun is treated as masculine if it refers to rational beings, and as feminine if it refers to non-rational beings; and this is open to question.
Where the grammarians differ, we refer you to the longer works.
An important observation:
Masculine and feminine with a plural are judged by its singular: if its singular is masculine we make the number feminine, and if its singular is feminine we make the number masculine.
الرهط: a group of three to ten people; it may be pluralised as أرهط and أراهط, with disagreement among the grammarians.

safi-cedvel:49-49.t:
* I'rab:
The fāʿil (agent) in (قالوا) refers to some of the people saying to others; (بالله) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تقاسموا); (اللام) is the lām of the oath; (نبيتنّه) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative; (أهله) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the object pronoun in (نبيّتنه); (ثمّ) is a conjunction; (لنقولنّ) is like لنبيّتنه; (لوليّه) is attached to (نقولنّ); (ما) is negating; (الواو) is a conjunction — or circumstantial —; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis.
The clause «قالوا» has no grammatical position: resumptive, explanatory.
The clause «تقاسموا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «نبيّتنّه ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath.
The clause «نقولنّ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer of the oath.
The clause «ما شهدنا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «إنّا لصادقون» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of شهدنا.].

* Rhetoric:
- تقاسموا:
فاعل and تفاعل: two forms of participation; each indicates that more than one person shared in the action, which is why it is called the form of participation.

safi-cedvel:50-53.t:
* I'rab:
(مكرا) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) in both places, for the two verbs; (الواو) is circumstantial; (لا) is negating.
The clause «مكروا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «مكرنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «هم لا يشعرون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «لا يشعرون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).
(51) (الفاء) is resumptive; (كيف) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كان; (أنّا) is a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its noun; (الواو) is a conjunction; (قومهم) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the object pronoun in (دمّرناهم); (أجمعين) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of meaning for the pronoun and for القوم, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ [Note: it may be a ḥāl of both.].
The clause «انظر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كان عاقبة..» is in the position of the accusative as the object of انظر, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative كيف.
The clause «دمّرناهم ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أنّا.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّا دمّرناهم ...) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) عاقبة, i.e. "بأنا دمّرناهم" [Note: it may be a badal (substitute) of عاقبة, in the position of the nominative ... or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي", the clause being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).].
(52) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (تلك) is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ, its khabar being بيوتهم; (خاوية) is an accusative ḥāl of البيوت, its governor being the demonstrative; (بما) is attached to خاوية, the bāʾ being causal and ما a maṣdar-forming particle; (في ذلك) is attached to the khabar of إنّ; (اللام) is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) for emphasis; (آية) is the accusative noun of إنّ; (لقوم) is attached to آية in the sense of admonition and lesson.
The clause «تلك بيوتهم ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause كان عاقبة [Note: the clause may be resumptive, and so have no grammatical position.].
The clause «ظلموا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لآية ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «يعلمون ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.
(53) (الواو) is a conjunction in both places; (الذين) is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), in the position of the accusative.
The clause «أنجينا ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause تلك بيوتهم.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «كانوا يتّقون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «يتّقون» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
Metaphor (al-istiʿāra): in the words of Allah the Exalted وَمَكَرْنا مَكْراً.
Allah's plotting is His destroying them from where they did not perceive. It is likened to the plotting of a plotter by way of metaphor.

* Benefits:
3- فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ ...
The making of the verb feminine or masculine has been mentioned already; in this āya the verb «كان» is masculine although the fāʿil (agent) «عاقبة» is feminine, but it is non-rational, and in this case the verb may be either feminine or masculine, so take note.
Making the verb feminine means attaching the tāʾ of the feminine at its end if it is past, and placing the imperfect-prefix tāʾ at its beginning if it is imperfect; making it masculine means omitting them. To complete this discussion you must return to it in its places, for it is a fascinating topic, worthy of study and verification.
1- We came across a short while ago the story of the band made up of nine men who conspired to kill Ṣāliḥ, and the cave fell upon them and killed them all.
2- Man plots; as for Allah, He does not plot. Plotting was attributed to Allah only for the sake of mushākala (correspondence), which is one of the devices of rhetoric that we have alluded to before. The definition of mushākala: it is mentioning a thing by the word for something else because it occurs in its company.
[Translator's note: the numbering of the Benefits (3, then 1, 2) is as in the source.]

safi-cedvel:54-55.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (لوطا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر"; (إذ) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb [Note: or a badal (substitute) of (لوطا), a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), in the sense of what Lūṭ said at that time.]; (لقومه) is attached to (قال); (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke; (الواو) is the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial) ...
The clause «(اذكر) لوطا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قال ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تأتون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
(55) (الهمزة) is mentioned to reinforce the disapproval; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (شهوة) is an accusative ḥāl of الرجال; (من دون) is attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent); (بل) is for digression (iḍrāb) and commencement ...
The clause إنّكم لتأتون ... has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a badal of the clause تأتون الفاحشة ...].
The clause «تأتون الرجال ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «أنتم قوم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تجهلون ...» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.
The clause «أنتم تبصرون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «تبصرون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) أنتم.

* Benefits:
From the stories of the Qur'an: «the story of Lūṭ» ...
Ibrāhīm departed from Egypt, taking Lūṭ with him on his journey, and they returned from that land with much wealth and abundant good, and settled in that Holy Land. But it became too narrow for their livestock and flocks, so Lūṭ moved away from the encampment of his uncle Ibrāhīm, and settled in the city of Sodom.
Its people were of corrupt morals and evil intentions; they did not refrain from disobedience, nor did they forbid one another from wrongdoing ... They invented an abomination in which none had preceded them: they used to come to males, and leave the women whom Allah had created for them.
[Translator's note: the source prints «الذاكران» here; in the repeated text under āyas 57-58 it reads «الذكران» (males), which is the sense translated.]
Allah revealed to Lūṭ that he should call them to the worship of Allah and that they should abandon the abominations they practised. But they put their fingers in their ears; their insight had been blinded and rust had been cast upon their hearts. They made threats to Lūṭ and those who believed with him, and resolved to drive them out of their town.
[Translator's note: the source here prints «فواعدوا» ("they made an appointment with"); the parallel text under āyas 57-58 has «فتوعدوا» ("they threatened"), which is the sense translated.]
Lūṭ asked his Lord to help him against these sinful people and to bring painful punishment upon them.
Allah answered his prayer and sent angels to this town whose people were wrongdoers, to bring upon them the worst of punishment. The messengers passed by Ibrāhīm first, told him of their mission and gave him glad tidings of a knowledgeable son.
Ibrāhīm feared for Lūṭ and those who believed with him, but the messengers reassured him and told him that Lūṭ and those who believed with him would not be struck by the punishment, and would be among those saved.
The messengers came to stay at Lūṭ's house, and the people heard of these guests who had come to Lūṭ's house. The angels were in the form of young men of the freshest build and the most beautiful faces, so Lūṭ's people coveted them and surrounded Lūṭ's house, wanting to reach his guests.
A cloud of grief covered Lūṭ, and a storm of anger seized him, as he saw the people storming his house and trying to assault his guests.
When the angels saw the grief and distress Lūṭ was in, they calmed his anxiety and stilled his fear, and said: O Lūṭ, we are the messengers of your Lord; we have come to rescue you and to repel the aggression from you, so these unbelievers will not reach you.
They commanded him to travel by night with his family, and to leave this town which Allah had decreed He would turn upside down.
Lūṭ went out with his family, and left the town and its people without regret for it. Then the command of Allah came to it: its land was shaken, it was turned upside down, and then it was covered with a rain of baked clay (sijjīl), so that their abode became a barren waste, and their houses empty because of their wrongdoing «إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً وَما كانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ».

* Morphology:
(60) حدائق: plural of حديقة, a noun for a garden with a wall around it; its pattern is فعيلة in the sense of مفعولة, because the wall surrounds (aḥdaqa) it.
(بهجة): a noun from (بهجه) meaning "he gladdened him", of the فتح class; it means beauty and freshness; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.
(61) حاجزا: active participle of the triliteral حجز; its pattern is فاعل.
(62) المضطر: passive participle of the five-letter اضطرّ; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn, and it contains the substitution (ibdāl) of the tāʾ by ṭāʾ ... see āya (126) of Sūrat al-Baqara.

* Rhetoric:
Iltifāt (shift of person): in the words of Allah the Exalted فَأَنْبَتْنا بِهِ حَدائِقَ ذاتَ بَهْجَةٍ.
A shift from the third person to the first person with the nūn of majesty, to emphasise that the action belongs exclusively — by way of contrast — to Him the Exalted Himself, and to announce that causing these gardens to grow, varied in kinds, qualities, colours, tastes, scents and shapes — with the consummate beauty and splendid radiance they possess — by a single water, is a mighty matter that none can accomplish but He alone, Mighty and Majestic.

* Benefits:
- The interrogative hamza:
We have spoken previously about some of the characteristics of the interrogative hamza, and here we shall complete the study of this hamza: it is the root of the interrogative particles; indeed it is — as Sībawayh said — "the interrogative particle that does not leave it for something else, and the interrogative originally has no other". They only left out the interrogative hamza in «من، ومتى، وهل» and the like because they were safe from ambiguity. For this reason it is distinguished by special rulings. The first of them: it may be omitted, whether it precedes «أم», as in the words of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
فوالله ما أدري وإن كنت داريا ... بسبع رمين الجمر أم بثمان
(By Allah, I do not know — though I am one who knows — whether they cast the pebbles with seven or with eight.)
He meant: أبسبع.
or does not precede أم, as in the words of al-Kumayt:
طربت وما شوقا إلى البيض أطرب ... ولا لعبا مني وذو الشيب يلعب
(I was moved — yet not out of longing for the fair ones am I moved, nor in play; and does the grey-haired man play?)
The second: it is used to request a conception (taṣawwur), e.g.:
«أخالد مقبل أم علي» ("Is it Khālid who is coming, or ʿAlī?").
And to request an assent (taṣdīq), e.g. «أمحمد قادم»؟ ("Is Muḥammad coming?"). The rest of the interrogative particles are restricted to requesting assent only.
[Translator's note: as printed; the usual statement in the grammar books is that هل alone is restricted to requesting assent, while the other interrogative nouns request conception.]
The third: it enters upon the affirmative, as already mentioned, and upon the negative, e.g. «أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ».
The fourth: its complete priority of position (taṣdīr): it is not mentioned after «أم», so we do not say: أقرأ خالد أم أكتب؟
But we say: أقرأ خالد أم هل كتب؟ ("Did Khālid read, or did he write?"). Likewise it precedes the conjunctions «الواو، أو الفاء، أو ثمّ», to draw attention to its being original in taking the first position, as in:
«أولم ينظروا» «أفلم يسيروا» «أثمّ إذا ما وقع آمنتم به»; whereas its sisters come after the conjunctions, e.g. «وكيف تفكرون، فأين تذهبون، فأنى تؤفكون، فأي الفريقين».
The fifth: the interrogative hamza differs from the others in many matters, and what is permitted with it is not permitted with the others:
1- An accusative noun may come after it, e.g. أعبد الله ضربته ("Is it ʿAbd Allāh whom you struck?") and أعمرا قتلت أخاه ("Is it ʿAmr whose brother you killed?"); in this case you imply a verb between the hamza and the accusative noun; and likewise: أزيدا مررت به أم عمرا ("Is it Zayd you passed by, or ʿAmr?").
2- The interrogative hamza entering upon the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl): when the interrogative hamza enters upon the connecting hamza, the interrogative hamza remains and the connecting hamza falls away, because the interrogative hamza takes the place of the connecting hamza in enabling the pronunciation of the quiescent letter, e.g.: أبن زيد أنت؟ ("Are you the son of Zayd?")
And e.g. «أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْعالِينَ» «أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ» «افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً». Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt said:
فقالت أبن قيس ذا ... وبعض الشيب يعجبها
(She said: "Is this Ibn Qays?" — and some grey hair pleases her.)
3- The interrogative hamza and the oath:
You say «آلله», asking a question together with emphasis by oath, and likewise «ايم الله» and «ايمن الله»; the interrogative hamza takes the place of the wāw of the oath, and the thing sworn by is made genitive by it. Here the connecting hamza in the Name of Majesty, or in «ايم» or «ايمن», is not dropped, but is made into a madda; it is here just as it would be if it entered upon something other than an oath. So you say: «آلرجل فعل ذلك» ("Was it the man who did that?"). The interrogative hamza here carries two meanings: interrogation and standing in for the wāw of the oath. So if you say «آلله لتفعلنّ», it is as though you had said:
«أتقسم بالله لتفعلنّ» ("Do you swear by Allah that you will surely do it?").
4- The interrogative hamza entering upon the definite article «ال»: when the interrogative hamza enters upon the definite article, the first is kept as a hamza and the second is turned into a madda, as in your saying: «آلرجل قال ذاك» ("Was it the man who said that?"); in writing, the alif stands for the two hamzas, e.g. «آلساعة جئت» ("Is it now that you have come?"). Of this kind are the words of Allah the Exalted:
«آللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ» «آلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ» «آلْآنَ وَقَدْ عَصَيْتَ قَبْلُ».
5- The hamza departing from genuine interrogation:
The hamza departs from genuine interrogation and is used for eight meanings.
a- Equivalence (taswiya): سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ.
b- Invalidating disapproval (al-inkār al-ibṭālī): e.g.: أَشَهِدُوا خَلْقَهُمْ؟ أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكافٍ عَبْدَهُ؟
c- Rebuking disapproval (al-inkār al-tawbīkhī): أَتَعْبُدُونَ ما تَنْحِتُونَ؟
d- Affirmation (taqrīr): e.g. أنصرت بكرا and أبكرا نصرت؟ ("Did you help Bakr?" / "Is it Bakr you helped?") e- Mockery (tahakkum), e.g.: قالُوا يا شُعَيْبُ أَصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا؟
And command, e.g.: «أَأَسْلَمْتُمْ», i.e. "submit!".
g- Wonder (taʿajjub), e.g.: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلى رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ.
h- Finding something slow (istibṭāʾ), e.g.: أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ؟
i- Iltifāt in His saying: «فَأَنْبَتْنا بِهِ حَدائِقَ ذاتَ بَهْجَةٍ» after His saying «أَمَّنْ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَأَنْزَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً»: in conveying the report He moved from the third person to speaking of Himself in the first person in His saying فأنبتنا. The secret of this is to emphasise that the action of causing growth belongs exclusively to Him the Exalted Himself, and to announce that causing gardens of different kinds to grow, with the ornaments of colour, the beauties of form, the varied tastes and the different scents of varying fragrance and perfume that appear in them — none of this can be accomplished except by an Able Creator, and He is Allah alone. For this reason He reinforced this exclusiveness by saying afterwards «ما كانَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تُنْبِتُوا شَجَرَها».
[Translator's note: the source announces eight meanings but lists items a–i, of which "the command" has no letter (it would be "f", و) and item i (iltifāt) is not a meaning of the hamza but repeats the Rhetoric section above.]

safi-cedvel:65-66.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) is negating; (من) is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of يعلم, in the position of the nominative [Note: it may be the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), with (الغيب) a badal (substitute) of the relative noun, and the fāʿil of يعلم being the word] [Translator's note: the footnote breaks off here in the source; presumably "the word (lafẓ) of the Name of Majesty" is meant.]; (في السموات) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من; (الغيب) is an accusative mafʿūl bihi; (إلّا) is for exception, meaning غير ("other than") [Note: or a particle of exception meaning لكن ("but"), so that the exception is discontinuous, because a continuous exception would imply that Allah is among those in the heavens and the earth, i.e. that He has a place ... On this view the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "يعلم الغيب".]; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, and it together with the إلّا before it is a nominative naʿt (adjective) of the relative noun [Note: it may be a badal of the relative noun if إلّا is not taken to mean غير, i.e. "no one knows the unseen except Allah".]; (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (أيّان) is an accusative adverb of time, its governor being (يبعثون), and the wāw in it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يعلم ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «ما يشعرون ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «يبعثون» is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يشعرون, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative أيّان; it carries the sense of يعرفون ("they know").
(66) (بل) is for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī) in the three places; (في الآخرة) is attached to (ادّارك); (في شكّ) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم); (منها) is attached to a naʿt of شكّ, and the second (منها) is attached to the khabar (عمون).
The clause «ادّارك علمهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم في شك منها ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم منها عمون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

safi-cedvel:67-68.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of disapproval; (إذا) is an adverb of the future containing the sense of a condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb explained by what follows, i.e. "أنخرج إذا كنّا ..." ("shall we be brought out when we have become ..."); (الواو) is a conjunction; (آباؤنا) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the attached pronoun that is the noun of كان [Note: the conjoining without an emphasising detached pronoun is permitted because of the separator (ترابا).], nominative; (الهمزة) is like the first; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis.
The clause «قال الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The conditional clause — its protasis and its apodosis — is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «كنّا..» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «إنّا لمخرجون» has no grammatical position: an explanation of the implied apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
(68) (اللام) is the lām of the oath for an implied oath, and (نا) is a pronoun, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive (وعدنا); (هذا) is a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (نحن) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as a tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached pronoun that is the nāʾib fāʿil; (آباؤنا) is conjoined to the attached pronoun (نا), nominative; (قبل) is a noun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, attached to (وعدنا); (إن) is negating; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أساطير) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هذا).
The clause «وعدنا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath.
The clause «إن هذا إلّا أساطير ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.

safi-cedvel:69-70.t:
* I'rab:
(في الأرض) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (سيروا); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (انظروا ... المجرمين): the i'rab of something similar has been given [Note: in āya (51) of this sūra, in Part Nineteen.].
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «سيروا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «انظروا ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause سيروا.
The clause «كان عاقبة ...» is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of looking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
(70) (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is the prohibitive lā, governing the jussive; (عليهم) is attached to the negated (تحزن); (في ضيق) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of تكن; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the resumptive pronoun being omitted, i.e. يمكرونه.], and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما يمكرون) is in the position of the genitive by (من), attached to ضيق.
The clause «لا تحزن ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قل.
The clause «لا تكن ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قل.
The clause «يمكرون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(ضيق): maṣdar of ضاق, of the ضرب class; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:71-71.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (متى) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هذا); (الوعد) is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative — or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) —, nominative; (كنتم) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «يقولون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «متى هذا الوعد ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «كنتم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

safi-cedvel:72-72.t:
* I'rab:
(عسى) is a complete (tāmm) past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يكون ...); the noun of يكون is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); (لكم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ردف), by making it carry the sense of قرب ("drew near") [Note: or the lām is redundant (zāʾida) and the second-person pronoun is its object ... In al-Qāmūs: ردفه, like سمع and نصر, means "he followed him".]; (بعض) is the nominative fāʿil of ردف; (الذي) is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi, in the position of the genitive.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «عسى أن يكون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «يكون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «ردف ... بعض ...» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of يكون.
The clause «تستعجلون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).

safi-cedvel:73-75.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (ذو) is a nominative khabar (predicate), the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (على الناس) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) فضل; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is negating.
The clause «إنّ ربّك لذو..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لكنّ أكثرهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لا يشكرون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of لكنّ.
(74) (الواو) is a conjunction; (اللام) is like the first; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the resumptive pronoun being omitted; (الواو) is a conjunction; the second (ما) is like the first and conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it ...
The clause «إنّ ربّك ليعلم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّ ربّك لذو ...
The clause «يعلم..» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «تكنّ صدورهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (ما).
The clause «يعلنون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
75 (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (غائبة) is genitive in form and nominative in position, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (في السماء) is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of غائبة; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (في كتاب) is attached to the khabar of غائبة ...
The clause «ما من غائبة..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّ ربّك لذو ...

* Morphology:
(غائبة): it has been said to be the active participle of the triliteral غاب, with the tāʾ added for intensiveness; it has been said to be a maṣdar (verbal noun) like العاقبة and العافية; and it has been said to be a noun, not an adjective, like النطيحة and الذبيحة. The pattern is فاعلة.

* Benefits:
- The kinds of tāʾ marbūṭa that attach to nouns:
a- It is a sign of the feminine, with rulings and details that we pass over for brevity, e.g. قائم and قائمة. Five patterns are excepted from taking this tāʾ:
1- فعول, e.g. امرأة جسور ("a bold woman") 2- فعيل, e.g. امرأة جريح ("a wounded woman") 3- مفعال, e.g. امرأة منحار ("a woman who slaughters much").
4- مفعيل, e.g. امرأة معطير ("a much-perfumed woman") 5- مفعل, e.g. امرأة مغشم ("a reckless woman"). In all these adjectives man and woman are alike in being without this tāʾ.
b- It is for separation (faṣl): the tāʾ of separation separates the singular from its genus, e.g. «ثمرة» ("a fruit"), and separates the genus from its singular, e.g. «كماة» ("truffles").
c- The tāʾ of compensation (ʿiwaḍ): it comes as compensation for the fāʾ of the noun when it is dropped, e.g. عدة, or its ʿayn, e.g. إقامة, or its lām, e.g. سنة.
d- The tāʾ of Arabicisation (taʿrīb): it comes in Arabicising foreign nouns.
e- The tāʾ of intensiveness (mubālagha): it attaches to an adjective to indicate intensiveness in it, e.g. راوية, نسّابة, علّامة, etc., for one who transmits much, one expert in genealogies, and one of much and abundant knowledge.

safi-cedvel:76-77.t:
* I'rab:
(على بني) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يقصّ), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, as it is attached (mulḥaq) to the masculine plural; (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (فيه) is attached to (يختلفون).
The clause «إنّ هذا القرآن ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يقصّ ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «هم فيه يختلفون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «يختلفون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هم.
(77) (الواو) is a conjunction; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (للمؤمنين) is attached to (رحمة). The clause «إنّه لهدى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:78-81.t:
* I'rab:
(بينهم) is an accusative adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يقضي); (بحكمه) is attached to (يقضي); (الواو) is a conjunction — or circumstantial —; (العليم) is a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هو ...
The clause «إن ربّك يقتضي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
[Translator's note: the source prints «يقتضي»; the word in the āya is يَقْضِي.]
The clause «يقضي ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «هو العزيز ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يقضي [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).].
(79) (الفاء) links to the apodosis of an implied condition; (على الله) is attached to (توكّل); (على الحقّ) is attached to the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «توكّل ...» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you want success, then put your trust ...".
The clause «إنّك على الحق ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
(80) (لا) is negating in both places; (الدعاء) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the second verb تسمع, and that of the first was omitted because the second indicates it; (ولّوا) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied on the alif, which is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (مدبرين) is a ḥāl that emphasises the content of the verb (ḥāl muʾakkida).
The clause «إنّك لا تسمع ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption containing a second reason for the trust.
The clause «لا تسمع ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «لا تسمع (the second) ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the first clause لا تسمع.
The clause «ولّوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi ... and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
(81) (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negating, functioning like ليس; (أنت) is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as the noun of ما; (هادي) is genitive in form and accusative in position, the khabar of ما; (العمي) is a genitive muḍāf ilayhi; (عن ضلالتهم) is attached to هادي, by making it carry the sense of صارف ("turning away"); (إن) is negating; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (من) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (بآياتنا) is attached to (يؤمن); (الفاء) is causal.
The clause «ما أنت بهادي ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنك لا تسمع.
The clause «إن تسمع إلّا من ...» has no grammatical position: a reason for what preceded.
The clause «يؤمن..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «هم مسلمون» has no grammatical position: causal.

* Rhetoric:
Completion (al-tatmīm): in the words of Allah the Exalted «إِذا وَلَّوْا مُدْبِرِينَ».
The negation is restricted in order to complete the simile and emphasise the negation: for they — besides being deaf to the call to the truth — turn away from the caller, turning their backs; and there is no doubt that the deaf man does not hear the call even when the caller faces his ear-hole, close to him, so how much less when he is behind him or far from him?

safi-cedvel:82-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (عليهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وقع); (لهم) is attached to (أخرجنا); (من الأرض) is attached to the verb أخرجنا; (بآياتنا) is attached to the negated (يوقنون).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّ الناس كانوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (تكلّمهم), i.e. "بأنّ الناس".
The clause «وقع القول ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أخرجنا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تكلّمهم» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of دابّة.
The clause «كانوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أنّ.
The clause «لا يوقنون» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

* Benefits:
- The Beast of the Earth (dābbat al-arḍ):
We have no text that specifies for us its kind and nature, and all that is required of us is to believe in the unseen as He, Glorified and Exalted, has informed of it; He knows best about it. It does not harm us to be ignorant of it, just as it does not benefit us to run after knowledge of it. It is enough for us to say about it, and about similar hidden matters, «Allah knows best about that».

safi-cedvel:83-84.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (يوم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أذكر"; (من كلّ) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (فوجا); (ممن) is attached to what the prepositional phrase (من كلّ) is attached to, because it is a badal (substitute) of it; (بآياتنا) is attached to (يكذّب); (الفاء) is a conjunction, and the wāw in (يوزعون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «(اذكر) يوم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نحشر ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يكذّب ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «هم يوزعون» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause نحشر.
The clause «يوزعون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of (هم).
(84) (حتّى) is a particle of commencement (ibtidāʾ); (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of reproach; (بآياتي) is attached to (كذّبتم); (بها) is attached to (تحيطوا); (علما) is an accusative tamyīz (specification); (أم) is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning بل; (ماذا) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being تعملون [Note: or (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and (ذا) a relative noun, the khabar, with the clause كنتم تعملون as the ṣila of ذا.].
The clause «جاؤوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «كذّبتم ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «لم تحيطوا ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl [Note: the clause may be circumstantial, adding to the rebuke, i.e. "did you deny them without understanding them or reflecting on them?"].
The clause «كنتم تعملون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تعملون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(فوج): a collective noun (ism jamʿ) meaning a group; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; the plural is أفواج and فؤوج with ḍamma on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:85-85.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (عليهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وقع); (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle; (الباء) is a preposition of causation; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لا) is negating.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما ظلموا ...) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (وقع).
The clause «وقع القول ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ظلموا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «هم لا ينطقون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لا ينطقون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هم.

safi-cedvel:86-86.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative of rebuke; (أنّا) is a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its noun; (اللام) is for causation (taʿlīl); (يسكنوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; (فيه) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يسكنوا).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّا جعلنا ...) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يروا.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يسكنوا) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (جعلنا); the second object of جعلنا is omitted, its implied form being "مظلما" [Note: the verb (جعلنا) may mean "we created", in which case nothing need be supplied.].
(الواو) is a conjunction; (النهار مبصرا) are conjoined to the first and second objects [Note: or they are the two objects of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned, the conjoining then being of clauses.]; (في ذلك) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; (اللام) is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) for emphasis; (آيات) is the accusative noun of إنّ, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (لقوم) is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of آيات.
The clause «يروا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جعلنا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «يسكنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يؤمنون ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of قوم.

* Benefits:
1- We have seen that «جعل», in one of its two uses, puts two objects in the accusative. This āya contains both uses of جعل: in the words of Allah the Exalted أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِيَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ it puts a single object in the accusative, namely الليل — unless we consider that the clause «لِيَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ» takes the place of the second object; and in the words of the Exalted وَالنَّهارَ مُبْصِراً, النهار is the first object and «مبصرا» the second object ... i.e. «وجعلنا النهار مبصرا».
2- Al-Zamakhsharī says, describing some words that Allah attributes to Himself: "Do you not see His saying «صنع الله» and «وعد الله» and «فطرة الله» — after He has marked them, by annexing them to Himself, with the mark of magnification — how it is followed by His saying: «الَّذِي أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ», «وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ صِبْغَةً», and «لا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ الْمِيعادَ», «لا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ»."

safi-cedvel:87-90.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (يوم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" [Note: or conjoined to the preceding adverb (يوم نحشر ...) in āya (83) of this sūra.]; (في الصور) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb ينفخ; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (في السموات) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من, and likewise (في الأرض) for the second relative noun; (إلّا) is a particle of exception; (من) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the excepted, and the fāʿil (agent) of (شاء) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", i.e. Allah; (الواو) is circumstantial; (كلّ) is a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: it indicates generality, and it is on the assumption of an implied muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. كلّهم.]; (داخرين) is an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of أتوه.
The clause «(اذكر) يوم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ينفخ في الصور ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi ...
The clause «فزع من ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause ينفخ ...
The past verb has the force of the imperfect because its occurrence is certain.
The clause «شاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third relative (من).
The clause «كلّ أتوه ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of those in the heavens and the earth.
The clause «أتوه ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (كلّ).
(88) (الواو) is a conjunction; (جامدة) is the second mafʿūl bihi, its governor being تحسبها; (الواو) is circumstantial; (مرّ) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); (صنع) is the accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the resumptive pronoun being omitted, i.e. تفعلونه.].
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما تفعلون) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to خبير.
The clause «ترى ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause ينفخ في الصور.
The clause «تحسبها ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of ترى.
The clause «هي تمرّ ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the latent pronoun in جامدة.
The clause «(صنعت) صنع ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أتقن ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «إنّه خبير ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «تفعلون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
(89) (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (بالحسنة) is attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of جاء, i.e. "bringing it"; (الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (له) is attached to the fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ خير; (منها) is attached to خير; (الواو) is circumstantial; (من فزع) is attached to (آمنون); (يومئذ) is attached to (آمنون).
The clause «من جاء ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «جاء بالحسنة ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «له خير ...» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «هم ... آمنون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl [Note: it may be conjoined to the resumptive clause, and so have no grammatical position.].
