(90) (من جاء بالسيّئة) is like من جاء بالحسنة; (الفاء) links to the apodosis; (وجوههم) is the nominative nāʾib fāʿil of the verb كبّت; (في النار) is attached to (كبّت); (هل) is an interrogative particle used for negation, and (الواو) in (تجزون) is the nāʾib fāʿil; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, the resumptive pronoun being omitted, i.e. تعملونه.
The clause «من جاء (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause من جاء (the first).
The clause «جاء بالسيّئة ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «كبّت وجوههم» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم", and the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «هل تجزون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech) of an implied verb of saying, and the implied saying is a ḥāl of the pronoun in وجوههم [Note: because the muḍāf is part of the muḍāf ilayhi.].
The clause «كنتم تعملون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «تعملون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(88) جامدة: feminine of جامد, the active participle of the triliteral جمد; its pattern is فاعل, and it is فاعلة.
(مرّ): maṣdar of the triliteral مرّ, of the نصر class; and there are two other maṣdars, namely مرور but He turned to the past tense to convey that the terror is certain and established, that it will come to pass without doubt, befalling the people of the heavens and the earth, because the past verb indicates the existence of the action and that it is a certainty.
[Translator's note: the text is disjointed in the source: only one of the "two other maṣdars" is named, and the sentence then continues with a rhetorical remark that belongs to the past verb فَفَزِعَ in āya 87. No «Rhetoric» heading precedes the following paragraph in the source.]
Antithesis (al-ṭibāq): in the words of Allah the Exalted وَتَرَى الْجِبالَ تَحْسَبُها جامِدَةً وَهِيَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحابِ.
A wondrous antithesis between stillness and rapid motion: He made what appears to the eye of the beholder like the mountain in its stillness and firmness, yet it is swift, passing along rapidly as the clouds pass. Such is the case of great bodies, numerous in number: when they move, their motion can scarcely be discerned.
Al-Zamakhsharī described these āyas eloquently, saying:
"Look at the eloquence of this speech, the beauty of its composition and arrangement, the firmness of its binding, the soundness of its explanation, and how each part takes hold of the waistband of another, as though it had been cast in a single mould. For some reason it has overwhelmed every power and silenced the most eloquent tongues. When a maṣdar like this comes after a piece of speech, it comes like a witness to its truth and a herald of its rightness, and to the fact that it could not have been otherwise than as it was."

* Benefits:
- مَنْ جاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ خَيْرٌ مِنْها: it is noticeable in this āya and in the one after it that the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) comes joined with the fāʾ, because the apodosis is a nominal clause. This invites us to repeat the cases in which the apodosis is joined with the fāʾ; someone has spared us the trouble by collecting them in this verse of poetry, saying:
اسمية طلبية وبجامد ... وبما ولن وقد وبالتسويف
(A nominal clause, a clause of request, and with a non-inflecting verb, and with ما, لن, قد and with the particle of futurity.)

safi-cedvel:91-92.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) is the restrictive (kāffa) and restricted (makfūfa); (التاء) is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle ...
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن أعبد) is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being أمرت.
(هذه) is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (البلدة) is a genitive badal (substitute) of the demonstrative; (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ربّ; (الواو) is parenthetical; (له) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) كلّ; (الواو) is a conjunction; (أن أكون) is like أن أعبد; (من المسلمين) is attached to the omitted khabar of أكون.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أكون) is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi, its governor being the second أمرت.
The clause «أمرت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: it may be in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech) of an implied verb of saying, i.e. "say to them: إنّما ..."].
The clause «أعبد ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «حرّمها ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «له كلّ ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «أمرت (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أمرت (the first).
The clause «أكون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
(92) (الواو) is a conjunction; (أن أتلو) is like أن أعبد; (الفاء) is resumptive; (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (اهتدى) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the implied fatḥa, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّما) is like the first; (لنفسه) is attached to (يهتدي); (الواو) is a conjunction; (من ضلّ) is like من اهتدى; (الفاء) links to the apodosis; (إنّما) is like the first; (من المنذرين) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنا.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أتلو ...) is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أن أكون).
The clause «أتلو ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third particle-relative (أن).
The clause «من اهتدى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اهتدى ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «إنّما يهتدي ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «من ضلّ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause من اهتدى.
The clause «ضلّ ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «قل ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أنا من المنذرين ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl, and the link with the condition is implied, i.e. "say to him".

* Rhetoric:
Precaution (al-iḥtirās): in the words of Allah the Exalted وَلَهُ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ:
A beautiful precaution. This device has been mentioned before: it is brought to ward off a misconception that the speech might give rise to. He, Glorified be He, connected His name with Makka to honour it and to mention its sanctity; and when He had connected His name with the town singled out for this honour, He followed this by attributing everything other than it to His dominion, to cut off the misconception that His dominion is restricted to the town referred to, and to draw attention to the fact that the first attribution was intended only for honour, not because it alone is the property of Allah the Exalted.

safi-cedvel:93-93.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction; (لله) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) الحمد; (السين) is a particle of futurity; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (الواو) is resumptive; (ما) is negating, functioning like ليس; (غافل) is genitive in form and accusative in position, the khabar of ما; the second (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the resumptive pronoun being omitted, i.e. تعملونه.].
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما تعملون) is in the position of the genitive by (عن), attached to (mutaʿalliq) غافل.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّما أمرت [Note: in āya (91) of this sūra.].
The clause «الحمد لله ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «سيريكم ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «تعرفونها ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause سيريكم.
The clause «ما ربّك بغافل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تعملون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).

* Benefits:
- At the close of Sūrat al-Naml we refer the reader to what al-Bāqillānī said in interpreting and analysing this sūra and the places of inimitability in it; he said about it what is fine to say, even though no one of power or might can attain the eloquence of the Qur'an. Whoever wishes may return to what al-Bāqillānī said when discussing the places of eloquence in this sūra.

safi-cedvel:15-26.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (قد) a particle of certainty (علما) second direct object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative (الواو) a conjunction (لله) attached to an omitted predicate (khabar) of the subject (mubtadaʾ) الحمد (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, an adjective (naʿt) of the name of Majesty (اللفظ الجلالة) (على كثير) attached to (فضّلنا), (من عباده) attached to an adjective of كثير.
Clause: «the implied oath …» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «آتينا …» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath.
Clause: «قالا …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied clause, that is: "so they acted upon what We had given them and said: Praise be to Allah …"
Clause: «الحمد لله …» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «فضّلنا …» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
(16) (الواو) a conjunction in all three places (أيّها) a vocative, a specified indefinite noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative «[Note: and (ها) is for attention (tanbīh) and has no grammatical position.]», (الناس) a badal (substitute) for أيّ - or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) - nominative in form (منطق) second direct object, accusative «[Note: the first object became the deputy agent of (علمنا).]» (من كلّ) attached to (أوتينا), (اللام) it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis (المبين) an adjective of الفضل, nominative.
Clause: «ورث سليمان …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
Clause: «قال …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ورث.
Clause: «the vocative and its response:» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «علّمنا …» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
Clause: «أوتينا …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the vocative.
Clause: «إنّ هذا لهو الفضل …» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
Clause: «هو الفضل …» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate (khabar) of إنّ.
(17) (الواو) a conjunction in all three places (لسليمان) attached to (حشر), (جنوده) deputy agent, nominative (من الجنّ) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of جنوده (الفاء) a conjunction, and the wāw in (يوزعون) is the deputy agent.
Clause: «حشر … جنوده» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال …
Clause: «هم يوزعون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause حشر …
Clause: «يوزعون» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the subject (هم).
(18) (حتى) a particle of commencement (على واد) attached to (أتوا), and the sign of the genitive is the implied kasra on the yāʾ, which was dropped for lightness (يا أيّها النمل) like يا أيّها الناس (لا) a negation «[Note: the verb after it came with the emphatic nūn, by analogy in form with the prohibitive lā.]», (يحطمنّكم) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative, and the nūn is the nūn of emphasis (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl (circumstance) (لا) a negation.
Clause: «أتوا …» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
Clause: «قالت نملة …» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
Clause: «the vocative and its response …» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «ادخلوا …» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
Clause: «لا يحطمنّكم سليمان» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
Clause: «هم لا يشعرون» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
Clause: «لا يشعرون» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the subject (هم).
(19) (الفاء) a conjunction (ضاحكا) a ḥāl of the agent of تبسّم, confirming the content of the verb «[Note: or an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because smiling is the beginning of laughter.]», (من قولها) attached to (ضاحكا) «[Note: or attached to (تبسّم).]» and the nūn in (أوزعني) is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) (التي) a relative noun in the position of an accusative, an adjective of نعمتك (عليّ) attached to (أنعمت), and likewise (على والديّ) because it is conjoined to the first.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أشكر …) is in the position of an accusative, second direct object, its governing word being أوزعني.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أعمل …) is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar.
(برحمتك) attached to a ḥāl of the object of أدخلني, that is: "clothed in Your mercy" (في عبادك) attached to (أدخلني).
Clause: «تبسّم …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قالت نملة.
Clause: «قال …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تبسّم.
Clause of the vocative and its response … is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech «[Note: it is permissible for the vocative clause to be a parenthetical clause of supplication, with the clause أوزعني being the quoted speech.]».
Clause: «أوزعني …» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
Clause: «أشكر …» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
Clause: «أنعمت …» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
Clause: «اعمل» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second particle-type relative (أن).
Clause: «ترضاه …» is in the position of an accusative, an adjective of (صالحا).
Clause: «أدخلني …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أوزعني.
(20) (الواو) a conjunction (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, a subject (mubtadaʾ) (لي).
attached to an omitted predicate of the subject (ما), (لا) a negation (أم) it is the detached (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning بل (من الغائبين) attached to an omitted predicate of كان.
Clause: «تفقد …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال «[Note: or it is resumptive, in the course of the story of Solomon, peace be upon him.]».
Clause: «قال …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تفقّد.
Clause: «ما لي …» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «لا أرى …» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl of the yāʾ in (لي).
Clause: «كان من الغائبين» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(21) (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath, in all three places (أعذّبنه) like يحطمنّكم, and likewise (أذبحنّه, يأتينيّ), (عذابا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, standing in for the maṣdar because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar) (أو) a conjunction in both places (بسلطان) attached to (يأتينّي) «[Note: or to a ḥāl of the agent of يأتيني, that is: "bringing clear authority".]».
Clause: «أعذّبنّه …» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath.
Clause: «أذبحنّه …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أعذّبنّه.
Clause: «يأتيني …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أعذّبنّه «[Note: the conjunction here is required by the art of i'rab; as for the meaning, the (أو) before it means إلّا, that is: "I will surely punish him unless he brings me …", or "I will surely slaughter him unless he brings me …"]».
(22) (الفاء) a conjunction (غير) an adverb of time or place «[Note: it may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being its description, that is: "a stay not long".]», accusative, attached to (مكث), (بما) attached to (أحطت) «[Note: (ما) is a relative or a described indefinite.]», (به) attached to (تحط), (من سبأ) attached to (جئتك), (بنبإ) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of جئتك, that is: "bringing news".
Clause: «مكث …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, that is:
"So the hoopoe came and stayed …"
Clause: «قال …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause مكث.
Clause: «أحطت …» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «لم تحط به» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما) «[Note: it may be in the position of a genitive, an adjective of the indefinite (ما).]».
Clause: «جئتك …» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause أحطت.
(23) (الواو) a conjunction in both places (من كلّ) attached to (أوتيت), (لها) attached to an omitted fronted predicate of the subject عرش.
Clause: «إنّي وجدت …» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «وجدت …» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of إنّ.
Clause: «تملكهم» is in the position of an accusative, an adjective of امرأة.
Clause: «أوتيت …» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause تملكهم «[Note: or in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl of the agent of تملكهم, with قد implied.]».
Clause: «لها عرش …» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause تملكهم.
(24) (الواو) a conjunction (قومها) conjoined to the pronoun object in (وجدتها), (للشمس) attached to (يسجدون), (من دون) attached to a ḥāl of الشمس (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl (لهم) attached to (زيّن), (الفاء) a conjunction (عن السبيل) attached to (صدّ) (الفاء) a conjunction connecting the effect with the cause (لا) a negation.
Clause: «وجدتها …» has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the quoted speech.
Clause: «يسجدون …» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl of the object of وجدت and what is conjoined to it.
Clause: «زيّن لهم الشيطان …» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl «[Note: it may be resumptive within the scope of the quoted speech.]».
Clause: «صدهم …» is conjoined to the clause زيّن …, in the position of an accusative.
Clause: «هم لا يهتدون» is conjoined to the clause صدّهم …, in the position of an accusative.
Clause: «لا يهتدون» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the subject (هم).
(25) (ألّا) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative, and the negating lā «[Note: or it is redundant, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of a genitive by an implied (إلى), attached to (يهتدون), that is: "they are not guided to prostration".]» (لله) attached to (يسجدوا), (الذي) a relative in the position of a genitive, an adjective of the name of Majesty (في السموات) attached to الخبء because it has the sense of المخبّأ (the hidden) «[Note: or attached to a ḥāl of it, if it is a name for the inanimate things that are hidden.]»
… (ما) a relative noun in the position of an accusative, a direct object.
The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا يسجدوا) is in the position of an accusative, a badal (substitute) for أعمالهم, that is: "Satan made the non-prostration seem fair to them …", and what lies between the badal and the substituted word is a parenthetical.
Clause: «يسجدوا …» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
Clause: «يخرج …» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
Clause: «يعلم …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يخرج.
Clause: «تخفون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما), and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted «[Note: it may be the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما), with no ʿāʾid to be implied.]».
Clause: «تعلنون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (ما), and the ʿāʾid is omitted.
(26) (إلّا) a particle of exception (هو) a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative, a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in the implied predicate موجود (ربّ) a badal for the detached pronoun, nominative «[Note: or هو is a second predicate of the subject (الله).]».
Clause: «الله لا إله إلّا هو …» has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the hoopoe's speech.
Clause: «لا إله إلّا هو» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the subject (الله).

* Morphology:
(16) منطق: a noun for every utterance by which one expresses what is in the mind; its wazn is مفعل, with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(18) النمل: a generic noun (ism jins) for the well-known animal; its singular is نملة; its wazn is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(19) ضاحكا: an active participle from the triliteral (ضحك); its wazn is فاعل.
(20) الهدهد: a generic noun for the well-known bird; its singular is هدهدة with ḍamma on both hāʾs and between them a dāl with sukūn, and (also) هدهدة with ḍamma, then kasra, then fatḥa, and هداهدة with ḍamma on the first hāʾ and kasra on the second hāʾ; the plural is هداهد on the pattern of عساكر, and هداهيد on the pattern of مفاتيح; the wazn of الهدهد is فعلل with ḍamma on the fāʾ and the lām and sukūn on the ʿayn, and it is also valid with ḍamma, then fatḥa, then kasra..
(22) سبأ: a proper noun for a land in the region of Yemen; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas.
(25) الخبء: a maṣdar of خبأ يخبأ (of the fatḥ class); in the verse the object (maf'ūl) is intended by it … or it is a name for what is hidden in earth or heaven.

* Rhetoric:
1- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in the saying of the Exalted وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ وَسُلَيْمانَ عِلْماً.
Partitiveness and diminution come from indefiniteness, and just as it comes to belittle the thing made indefinite, so it comes also to magnify it. The apparent sense of His saying «وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ وَسُلَيْمانَ عِلْماً», in the context of conferring favour, is a magnification of the knowledge they were given, as if He had said: "knowledge, and what knowledge!" And so it is, for their knowledge was of the kind that is deemed great and astonishing, among it the knowledge of the speech of birds and all the animals, which Allah the Exalted singled them out with; and all knowledge, relative to the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, is little and slight.
2- The use of a preposition: in the saying of the Exalted حَتَّى إِذا أَتَوْا عَلى وادِ النَّمْلِ.
He made أتوا transitive with على because the coming was from above, so he used the preposition of elevation. Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī gazed at this lofty sky and said:
فلشد ما جاوزت قدرك صاعدا ... ولشدّ ما قربت عليك الأنجم
(How greatly you have surpassed your station in ascending, and how greatly the stars have drawn near to you.)
And he said «عليك», not «إليك», because the nearness of the stars is from the direction of height.
3- The representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in the saying of the Exalted قالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يا أَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَساكِنَكُمْ لا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمانُ وَجُنُودُهُ وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ.
It is as if, when she saw them heading for the valley, she fled from them for fear of destruction, and another followed her, and she cried out a cry by which she alerted the ants around her, and they followed her. This was likened to the addressing and advising of rational beings, and for that reason they were treated as such, since she was made the speaker and the rest of the ants the ones addressed; so the speech comes out in the form of a representative metaphor, and it is permissible that it be an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya).
4- Jinās al-taṣrīf (paronomasia of inflection): in the saying of the Exalted وَجِئْتُكَ مِنْ سَبَإٍ بِنَبَإٍ يَقِينٍ:
Jinās al-taṣrīf is the difference in form between two words through the substitution of one letter for another, either from the same point of articulation or one close to it. It is among the beauties of speech connected with the wording, on condition that it comes naturally, or is fashioned by one who knows the essence of speech, preserving with it the soundness and rightness of the meaning. Here it has come with more than soundness, and so it is beautiful, and is novel in wording and meaning. Do you not see that had «بخبر» been put in place of «بنبإ» the meaning would have been sound, yet as it has come it is sounder, because of the added sense in النبأ (news of weight) which corresponds to the description of the situation.

* Benefits:
1- The speech of the birds:
Muqātil said - and I think he took his statement from the Isrāʾīliyyāt: Solomon was sitting in his camp, whose area was a hundred farsakhs by a hundred, twenty-five for the jinn, twenty-five for mankind, twenty-five for the birds and twenty-five for the wild beasts; and the jinn had woven for him a carpet of gold and silk, a farsakh by a farsakh. He saw a nightingale on a tree and said to his companions: "Do you know what this bird says?" They said: "Allah and His Prophet know best." He said: "It says: I have eaten half a fruit, so let the world be effaced." And a hoopoe passed over a tree, and he said: "Seek forgiveness of Allah, you sinners."
And a female bird cried out, and he told them that it was saying: "Would that these creatures had not been created." A peacock cried out, and he said it was saying: "As you judge, so shall you be judged." A swallow cried out, and he said it was saying: "Send forward good, you will find it." A ṭayṭawī cried out, and he said it was saying: "Glory be to my Lord the Most High." And the kite (as he went along) was saying: "Everything will perish except His Face."
The sandgrouse says: "Whoever keeps silent is safe." The parrot says: "Woe to him whose concern is the world." The rooster says: "Remember Allah, you heedless ones." The vulture says: "Son of Adam, live as you wish, your end is death." The eagle says: "In distance from people there is companionship." The frog says: "Glory be to my Lord the Most High …!"
2- A questioner asked: What made Solomon laugh?
The answer came: What made him laugh was two things:
The first: the ant's acknowledgement of his mercy and the mercy of his troops, and her saying وهم لا يشعرون, for had they perceived, they would not have done it.
The second: his delight at what Allah had given him, namely his understanding of the language of the ant, small and humble as she is.
3- The ḥāl is of two kinds:
explanatory (mubayyina) and confirmatory (muʾakkida):
a- The explanatory ḥāl: that whose meaning cannot be gathered without it, such as «جاء خالد راكبا»: the meaning of riding is not gathered except by mentioning the ḥāl «راكبا».
b- The confirmatory: that whose meaning is gathered without mentioning it, and it has several types: we pass over them and refer the reader to the longer books of grammar.
4- Sabaʾ:
It is a land lying in the south-west of the Arabian Peninsula, in the land of Yemen. It is mentioned in the books of the Old Testament and in the writings of the Arabs and the Greeks, and it is said that it was of great civilisation, and that its people traded in gold, silver and precious stones.
5- Bilqīs: she is the daughter of Sharāḥīl ibn Abī Sarj ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Qays ibn Ṣayfī ibn Sabaʾ; and it is said that her father was one of the great kings.
Sabaʾ is the father of the Yemeni tribes that were scattered after the incident of the Maʾrib dam.
6- al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfa agreed that the prostrations of the Qur'an are fourteen. They differed over the prostration of Ṣād and the two prostrations of al-Ḥajj.
7- The story of the flood of al-ʿArim:
Among the legends of the Arabs: that Sabaʾ is the father of the Arab tribes scattered because of the Maʾrib dam.
Sabaʾ was among the finest and most fertile of Allah's lands, the richest in trees and water; Allah mentioned that it was two gardens, on the right and on the left, and it was a month's journey for a diligent rider, travelling through gardens from its beginning to its end, with the sun never meeting him nor the shade leaving him, along with flowing water, clear air and wide open space. They remained as long as Allah willed, no king opposing them but they broke him. In the beginning of time floods would overrun their land, so the king of Ḥimyar gathered the people of his kingdom and consulted them about warding off the flood; they agreed to dig channels for it to lead it to the sea. He mobilised the people of his kingdom until he diverted the water, and built a dam at the place where the water flowed down from the mountains, paving it with stones and iron, and made in it conduits for the water of a cubit's circumference; when the flood came, its water was distributed through the conduits to their gardens and crops, by a measure whose benefit reached them all. When the kingship passed to ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir, whose brother ʿImrān was a soothsayer, a woman soothsayer called Ẓarīfa came to him and told him of the imminent failure of the dam and the surge of the flood, and warned him; so he gathered the people of Maʾrib, made food for them, informed them of the matter of the flood, and they agreed to depart.

safi-cedvel:27-28.t:
* I'rab:
(السين) a particle of futurity (الهمزة) for interrogation (أم) it is the connected (muttaṣila) one, balancing the interrogative hamza (من الكاذبين) attached to the predicate of كنت.
Clause: «قال …» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «سننظر …» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «صدقت …» is in the position of an accusative, the object of ننظر, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
Clause: «كنت من الكاذبين» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause صدقت.
(28) (بكتابي) attached to (اذهب) «[Note: or to an omitted ḥāl of the agent of اذهب.]», (هذا) an ʿaṭf bayān of كتابي - or a badal for it - in the position of a genitive (الفاء) a conjunction (إليهم) attached to (ألقه), (ثم) a conjunction (عنهم) attached to (تولّ), (الفاء) a conjunction (ماذا) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, a direct object, its governing word being يرجعون «[Note: or (ما) is an interrogative noun, a subject, (ذا) a relative noun, a predicate, and the clause يرجعون is the ṣila, and the interrogative sentence is in the position of an accusative, the object of انظر, which is suspended by the interrogative.]», containing the sense of "what answer they return".
Clause: «اذهب …» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «ألقه …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause اذهب.
Clause: «تولّ …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ألقه.
Clause: «انظر …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تولّ.
Clause: «يرجعون …» is in the position of an accusative, a direct object, its governing word being انظر, which is suspended by the interrogative.

* Morphology:
(28) تولّ: it has an ʿilāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, for the sake of the indeclinable form; its imperfect is (يتولّى), its wazn is تفعّ.

safi-cedvel:29-31.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) a vocative, a specified indefinite noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative … and ها is for attention (الملأ) a badal for أيّ, nominative in form (إليّ) attached to (ألقي), (كتاب) deputy agent, nominative.
Clause: «قالت..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «the vocative and its response..» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «إنّي ألقي ...» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
Clause: «ألقي إليّ كتاب ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of إنّ.
(30) (من سليمان) attached to an omitted predicate of إنّ (بسم) attached to an omitted word, its implied form being "my beginning" «[Note: or attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being (أبدأ).]» ...
Clause: «إنّه من سليمان» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «إنّه بسم ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنّه من سليمان.
Clause: «(ابتدائي) بسم الله ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of إنّ.
(31) (ألّا) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative, and a negative particle «[Note: it is permissible that (أن) be a particle of explanation, and (لا) a prohibitive, and the imperfect after it jussive..
It is preferable that they be written separately.]», (عليّ) attached to (تعلوا), (الواو) a conjunction, and the nūn in (ائتوني) is the nūn of protection (مسلمين) an accusative ḥāl of the agent of ائتوني.
The interpreted maṣdar (ألا تعلوا ...) is in the position of an accusative, being (mafʿūl bihi) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "I ask" - that is: "I ask that there be no exalting yourselves against me" «[Note: it is permissible that it be in the position of a nominative, the predicate of an omitted subject, its implied form being "it is".]».
Clause: «تعلوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن) «[Note: the clause may be explicative if (لا) is parsed as prohibitive.]».
Clause: «(أطلب) عدم العلوّ» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «ائتوني ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the explanatory resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(آيات) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ تلك, nominative, and the pointing is to the verses of the sūra (الواو) is a conjunction (كتاب) is conjoined to القرآن, genitive.
The clause: «تلك آيات القرآن ... » has no grammatical position; it is an initial clause (ibtidāʾiyya) ...
(2-3) (هدى) is a second khabar, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma [Note: it is permissible that it be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هي ... or a ḥāl from آيات, and the sign of the accusative is the implied fatḥa.], (للمؤمنين) is attached to ببشرى, (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of genitive, a naʿt of للمؤمنين [Note: or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هم ...], (الواو) is a conjunction, or of ḥāl (هم), the second, is in the position of nominative, tawkīd of the first (بالآخرة) is attached to (يوقنون).
And the clause: «يقيمون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause: «يؤتون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «هم ... يوقنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause [Note: or it is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يقيمون and يؤتون.].
And the clause: «يوقنون ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Rhetoric:
1- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in His saying, the Exalted, وَكِتابٍ مُبِينٍ:
He made "the clear Book" indefinite so as to leave it vague through indefiniteness, which makes it more majestic, as in His saying, the Exalted, فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ مَلِيكٍ مُقْتَدِرٍ. As for His conjoining it to القرآن although it is the Qur'an itself, it is of the kind of conjoining one attribute to another, as you say: "This is the deed of the generous and the open-handed, the noble," because the Qur'an is that which is sent down, blessed, confirming what is before it, so its ruling is that of attributes independent in praise.
2- Repetition of the pronoun: in His saying, the Exalted, وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ.
He repeated the pronoun, so that the meaning of the speech became: "None is certain of the Hereafter with true certainty except these, who combine faith and righteous action," because fear of the Hereafter moves them to bear hardships.
3- Expression by nominal and verbal sentence: in His saying, the Exalted, الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ. Faith and certainty in the Hereafter are a fixed matter whose continuance is required, and for that reason He brought it as a nominal sentence and made its khabar an imperfect verb, saying «وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ», to indicate that their certainty continues in a renewing manner. As for establishing prayer and giving zakat, they recur and renew in their appointed times, and for that reason He brought them as two verbs, saying الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ.

safi-cedvel:4-5.t:
* I'rab:
(بالآخرة) is attached to (لا يؤمنون), (لهم) is attached to (زيّنا), (الفاء) is a conjunction.
The clause: «إنّ الذين.. زيّنا» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause: «زيّنا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause: «هم يعمهون» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause زيّنا ...
And the clause: «يعمهون ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(5) (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ, its khabar is (الذين), (لهم) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (سوء), (هم ... الأخسرون) is like (هم ... يوقنون ... ) [Note: in the preceding verse.].
And the clause: «أولئك الذين ... » is in the position of nominative, a second khabar of (إنّ).
And the clause: «لهم سوء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second (الذين).
And the clause: «هم ... الأخسرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لهم سوء [Note: it is permissible that it be conjoined to the clause أولئك الذين, or conjoined to the relative, the khabar of أولئك.].

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (اللام) is the shifted lām, and the nāʾib fāʿil in (تلقّي) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (من لدن) is attached to (تلقّي).
The clause: «إنّك لتلقّى ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «تلقّى ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ ...

* Morphology:
(تلقّى), it has a weakening by substitution (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its origin is تلقّي, the yāʾ having come with a vowel after a fatḥa and been changed to alif, and it is written short with an undotted yāʾ because it is fifth (in the letters of the root and augments).

safi-cedvel:7-8.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ) is an adverbial noun in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (لأهله) is attached to (قال), (السين) is a particle of futurity (منها) is attached to the first (آتيكم) [Note: or to a ḥāl from خبر, a naʿt which has been fronted before the thing qualified.], (بخبر) is attached to the first (آتيكم) (بشهاب) is attached to the second (آتيكم) (قبس) is a badal of شهاب, genitive [Note: it is permissible that it be a naʿt of it, of the kind of description by a maṣdar.].
The clause: «قال موسى ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi ... and the implied clause اذكر has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «إني آنست..» is in the position of accusative, the reported speech.
And the clause: «آنست نارا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause: «سآتيكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive clause.
And the clause: «آتيكم (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آتيكم (the first).
And the clause: «لعلّكم تصطلون» has no grammatical position; it is causal, or an explanatory resumptive clause. And the clause: «تصطلون ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of لعلّ.
(2) [Translator's note: the source prints "(2)" here, apparently a misprint for (8), the next verse.] (الفاء) is a conjunction (لمّا) is an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to the apodosis نودي, and the nāʾib fāʿil in (نودي) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", that is, Mūsā [Note: it is permissible that the nāʾib fāʿil be the interpreted maṣdar أن بورك ... or the pronoun of the maṣdar understood from the verb, that is, "the call".], (أن) is a particle of explanation [Note: preceded by a verb with the meaning of speaking but not its letters ... or it is a maṣdar particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive through an omitted preposition, that is, بأن بورك, attached to (نودي) ...
and it is permissible that it be the lightened form of the heavy (anna), its ism being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), that is, بأنّه بورك من في النار ...], (من) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, nāʾib fāʿil (في النار) is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative (من), (من حولها) is like من في النار and conjoined to it, (الواو) is resumptive (سبحان) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, its implied form being نسبّح (ربّ) is a naʿt of the divine name, genitive like it ...
And the clause: «جاءها ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «نودي ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
And the clause: «بورك ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative..
And the clause: «(نسبّح) سبحان ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive ...

* Morphology:
(تصطلون), it has the substitution of the tāʾ of the form iftiʿāl with ṭāʾ; its origin is تصتلون, and when the tāʾ came after the ṣād it was changed to ṭāʾ.
(بورك), it has the change of the alif to wāw because it is silent and what precedes it is vowelled with ḍamma, to suit the passive.

* Rhetoric:
The use of «أو» instead of the wāw: in His saying, the Exalted, سَآتِيكُمْ مِنْها بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ آتِيكُمْ بِشِهابٍ.
He preferred «أو» to the wāw for a splendid rhetorical point, for «أو» gives the sense of choice, and he built his hope on the basis that if he did not obtain both of his needs, he would not lack one of them: either guidance on the road, or taking a brand of fire, out of self-effacement and an acknowledgement of his shortcoming toward his Lord.

* Benefits:
- تصطلون:
The origin of the word is تصتلون. But according to the rule that always tends to ease pronunciation, when the tāʾ fell after the ṣād, one of them light and the second heavy, difficulty in moving from one to the other arose, because the two points of articulation are distant from each other, which required changing the tāʾ to ṭāʾ so that the two points of articulation would be united or close, and consequently they would be easy to pronounce. So consider ... !

safi-cedvel:9-12.t:
* I'rab:
(موسى) is a vocative, a single proper noun, indeclinable on the implied ḍamma, in the position of accusative, and the (الهاء) in (انّه) is the pronoun of the matter, in the position of accusative, the ism of إنّ (العزيز) is a naʿt of the divine name, nominative (الحكيم) is a second naʿt, nominative.
The clause: «النداء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّه أنا الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «أنا الله ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
(10) (الواو) is a conjunction and (الفاء) likewise (لمّا) is an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to the apodosis (ولّى), (مدبرا) is an accusative ḥāl confirming the content of its governing verb (الواو) is a conjunction (لا) is a prohibitive jussive particle, and the second is a negative (لديّ) is an adverb, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to the negated (يخاف). And the second yāʾ of the doubled one is in the position of genitive by annexation.
And the clause: «ألق ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «رآها ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «تهتزّ..» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the object of رآها.
And the clause: «كأنّها جانّ ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil of تهتزّ [Note: or a second ḥāl from the object.].
And the clause: «ولّى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
And the clause: «لم يعقّب ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the apodosis of the condition.
And the second clause of the call is in the position of accusative, the reported speech of an implied saying.
And the clause: «لا تخف ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «إنّي لا يخاف ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive clause, or causal; and the clause: «لا يخاف ... المرسلون ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
(11) (إلّا) is a particle of exception [Note: or a particle meaning (لكن).], (من) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as a discontinuous exception [Note: or in the position of nominative, a badal of (المرسلون), and it is permissible that (من) be a conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause ظلم ...], (ثمّ) is a conjunction (حسنا) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative (بعد) is an adverb, accusative, attached to (بدّل), (الفاء) is causal (رحيم) is a second khabar, nominative.
And the clause: «ظلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «بدّل» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ظلم.
And the clause: «إنّي غفور ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal for something implied, that is, "so I forgive him, for I am Forgiving" [Note: or it is a reason for the implied apodosis of the condition, whose implied form is "so I forgive him".].
(12) (الواو) is a conjunction (في جيبك) is attached to (أدخل), (تخرج) is an imperfect jussive, the response to the request (بيضاء) is an accusative ḥāl (من غير) is attached to a second ḥāl from the fāʿil of تخرج (في تسع) is attached to a third ḥāl from the fāʿil of تخرج, that is, "a sign among nine signs" [Note: or attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being اذهب ...], (إلى فرعون) is attached to a ḥāl from تسع آيات [Note: it is permissible to attach it to the implied verb اذهب ...], (فاسقين) is a naʿt of (قوما), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
And the clause: «أدخل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لا تخف [Note: and accordingly what is between the two clauses is parenthetical.].
And the clause: «تخرج ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of an implied condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ, that is: "if you put your hand in ... it will come out ...".
And the clause: «إنّهم كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive clause.
And the clause: «كانوا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:13-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive (لمّا جاءتهم) is like لمّا رآها [Note: in verse (10) of this sūra.], (مبصرة) is an accusative ḥāl from آياتنا.
And the clause: «جاءتهم آياتنا ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
And the clause: «هذا سحر ... » is in the position of accusative, the reported speech.
(14) (الواو) is a conjunction (بها) is attached to (جحدوا), (الواو) is of ḥāl (ظلما) is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl [Note: that is, "being wrongdoers", so the governing element in it is the verb جحدوا ... and it is permissible that (ظلما) be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, that is, "they denied them because of their wrongdoing".], accusative (الفاء) is resumptive (كيف) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, the khabar of كان.
And the clause: «جحدوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
And the clause: «استيقنتها أنفسهم ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil of جحدوا, with an implied قد.
And the clause: «انظر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «كان عاقبة ... » is in the position of accusative, the object of "looking", or with an implied preposition, and the verb has been suspended by the interrogative.

* Morphology:
(مبصرة), feminine of مبصر, an active participle from the quadriliteral أبصر, in the sense of the passive, by way of rational metaphor (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī).

* Rhetoric:
The imaginative implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-takhyīliyya): in His saying, the Exalted, فَلَمَّا جاءَتْهُمْ آياتُنا مُبْصِرَةً.
He made sight theirs, though it is in reality for those who contemplate them, because of the connection between them and the people, for they see only by reason of their contemplating them, so the attribution is figurative, of the kind of attribution to the cause.
It is also possible to make the signs as though they see and so guide, because the blind are unable to be guided, let alone guide others, so that there would be in the speech an implicit imaginative metaphor, embellished (murashshaha).
